summary: The decision that matters most is in Transportation: sign for 6 new crews by December 31, 2024, so they train in January and work from February. That department alone accounts for $4.62M of the net savings. Across the four departments the plan spends $3.16M more on crew payroll than keeping January's crews all year, and avoids $9.35M in overdue and year-end backlog costs: an expected 2025 cost of $15.62M against $21.81M, a net $6.19M less. It costs $410k more than the cheapest plan; that difference buys at least 90% on time at every planning level (demand 14% under to 14% over forecast). Crews grow as follows: Public Works from 50 to 70 crews by Aug, Transportation from 18 to 26 crews by May, Parks from 10 to 12 crews by Jun, and Inspectional Services from 16 to 19 crews by Jul. Two cautions. The on-time rates in this report are what crew capacity allows under the brief's assumptions, not forecasts of the city's measured rates. And most of Inspectional Services' lateness comes from inspection and legal process, which more crews will not fix.
